Convert a tidy tibble into a format compatible with the "Functional Analysis" module in 'MetaboAnalyst'

Source: R/convert.R
convert_to_fa.Rd

Creates a tibble with columns m.z, p.value, t.score and optionally r.t to use in the "Functional Analysis" module in 'MetaboAnalyst'. Metrics are calculated using a t.test.

Usage

convert_to_fa(
  data,
  m_z_col,
  rt_col = NULL,
  group_column,
  groups_to_compare,
  batch_column = NULL,
  batch = NULL,
  adjust_p = FALSE,
  log2_before = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A tidy tibble created by read_featuretable.

m_z_col

Which column holds the precursor m/z? Uses args_data_masking.

rt_col

Optional. Which column holds the precursor retention times? Uses args_data_masking.

group_column

Which column should be used for grouping? Usually group_column = Group. Uses args_data_masking.

groups_to_compare

Names of the groups which should be compared as a character vector. Those are the group names in the group_column. They are usually provided in the form of a metadata tibble and joined via join_metadata.

batch_column

Which column contains the batch information? Usually batch_column = Batch. Only relevant if data contains multiple batches. For example, if data contains 2 batches and each batch contains measurements of separate controls, group_column and batch arguments should be provided. Otherwise controls of both batches will be considered when calculating the p-value and log2 fold change. Uses args_data_masking.

batch

The names of the batch(es) that should be included when calculating p-value and log2 fold change.

adjust_p

Should the p-value be adjusted? Can be either FALSE, (the default) in case no adjustment should be made or any or the name from p.adjust.methods (e.g., adjust_p = "fdr").

log2_before

A logical. Should the data be log2 transformed prior to calculating the p-values?

...

Arguments passed on to t.test. If none are provided (the default), a Welch Two Sample t-test will be performed.

Value

A tibble with columns m.z, p.value, t.score and optionally r.t.

Examples

# Without optional retention time column
toy_metaboscape %>%
  join_metadata(toy_metaboscape_metadata) %>%
  convert_to_fa(group_column = Group,
                groups_to_compare = c("control", "treatment"),
                return_tbl = TRUE,
                alternative = "two.sided",
                m_z_col = `m/z`)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#>      m.z  p.value t.score
#>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1  162.  0.0175   -8.04 
#>  2  277.  0.200     1.58 
#>  3  305.  0.0111  -10.3  
#>  4  418.  0.798     0.311
#>  5  105.  0.182    -1.75 
#>  6  106.  0.781     0.311
#>  7  238. NA        NA    
#>  8  746.  0.561    -0.655
#>  9  428.  0.00106  -8.49 
#> 10 1285. NA        NA    

# With optional retention time column
toy_metaboscape %>%
  join_metadata(toy_metaboscape_metadata) %>%
  convert_to_fa(group_column = Group,
                groups_to_compare = c("control", "treatment"),
                return_tbl = TRUE,
                m_z_col = `m/z`,
                rt_col = RT)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>      m.z  p.value t.score   r.t
#>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1  162.  0.0175   -8.04   0.45
#>  2  277.  0.200     1.58   0.45
#>  3  305.  0.0111  -10.3    0.55
#>  4  418.  0.798     0.311  1   
#>  5  105.  0.182    -1.75   2.84
#>  6  106.  0.781     0.311  3.33
#>  7  238. NA        NA      5.22
#>  8  746.  0.561    -0.655  6.37
#>  9  428.  0.00106  -8.49   7.08
#> 10 1285. NA        NA      8.32
